chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi and Muawiya ibn Ammar, all together, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
He said: It does not harm you whether you enter into Ihram at night or by day, except that the superior of that is at the decline of the sun.

key_terms.أَحْرَمْتَ: You entered into the state of Ihram

ai.seo_question: When is the best time to enter Ihram for Hajj?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the validity of entering the state of Ihram is not contingent upon the time of day, as either night or day suffices, but establishes a strong preference (fadilah) for performing it at Zawal (midday). This ruling aligns with the Prophetic practice of avoiding extreme heat or darkness for ritual preparations, reflecting the Shia scholarly emphasis on following the Imams' guidance on the optimal conditions for worship. The distinction between validity and preference underscores the flexibility in Islamic jurisprudence while encouraging believers to seek the most auspicious times for their devotions.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, form Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, and Muawiya Bin Ammar, altogether, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>
having said: ‘It does not harm you whether you wear Ihraam at night or by the day, except that the superior of that is at the (start of the) decline of the sun’.
en.sarwar: 1. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘ Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Am mar all have said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
It is not harmful to assume the state of Ihram during the night or during the day; however, it is more virtuous to do so at Zawal (declining of the sun toward the west at noontime).’”
